anomalies.observed: The two 120Ω CAN termination resistors are switched to the wrong CAN differential pairs. R34 is tied to /CAN0_N on pin 1 and to SW6 pin 1 on pin 2, while SW6 pin 3 is on /CAN1_P; R35 is tied to /CAN1_N on pin 1 and to SW6 pin 2 on pin 2, while SW6 pin 4 is on /CAN0_P. With the normal two-row DIP-switch pin mapping used by SW7, closing SW6 connects /CAN0_N/R34 to /CAN1_P and /CAN1_N/R35 to /CAN0_P, cross-coupling the two CAN buses instead of terminating each bus separately.
anomalies.expected: R34 should switch between its own /CAN0_N and /CAN0_P, and R35 should switch between its own /CAN1_N and /CAN1_P, so CAN0 and CAN1 remain separate buses as described by the specification.
anomalies.impact: If the termination switches are used, the two CAN buses are loaded together through 120Ω resistors and can be shorted/cross-coupled, causing bus errors and defeating the intended separation/isolation of CAN0 and CAN1.

anomalies.observed: Net /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW contains only the anodes of LEDs D4, D14, and D23. It has no connection to +3V3, 5V_switched, a driver, switch, jumper, or any other power/control node.
anomalies.expected: LED anode nets should be connected to a supply or LED-power driver so the LEDs can conduct through their cathode-side current-limit resistors and sink/level-shift logic.
anomalies.impact: The affected status/Ethernet/power LEDs cannot light because their common anode net is floating.

anomalies.observed: Both GND1 and GND2 pins of the isolated CAN transceivers U10 and U11 are connected to the common board GND net.
anomalies.expected: For an isolated CAN transceiver, GND1 and GND2 should be separate isolated ground domains; tying them to common GND removes galvanic isolation between the logic side and the CAN bus side.
anomalies.impact: The CAN interfaces are not galvanically isolated as described, exposing the CM4/logic ground to the CAN bus ground and allowing ground loops.
